story: Ravana, king of Lanka, was a great scholar of the Vedas, a master of music and medicine, and one of Shiva's greatest devotees. Furious when Lakshmana disfigured his sister Shurpanakha, he abducted Sita and refused every chance to return her, which led to the war and his death at Rama's hands.
belief: Most Hindus see him as the villain of the Ramayana, and his effigies are burned on Dussehra. But some places in India and Sri Lanka honour him as a great king and devotee.
turns: He ignored the warnings of his wife Mandodari, his brother Vibhishana and his own elders. He held Sita for months, chose war out of pride, and lost his sons and brothers before he fell himself.
facts: He is said to have composed the Shiva Tandava Stotram.
His ten heads are often read as the ten senses, or as mastery of ten branches of knowledge.
He carried a curse that he would die if he forced himself on an unwilling woman, which kept Sita safe.
